{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. A candidate class, generated during root-cause on the proj:chama field report of 2026-09-02 and stated so it can be refuted.

THREE OF THAT REPORT'S SIX FINDINGS ARE THE SAME SHAPE: a reflow2 self-description that is out of step with what the code does.

① `loop_status` — "1 answered question(s) never reached the design". The computation is `questions.iter().filter(|q| q.status == "answered").count()`. It knows the question is answered and its gap is open; the message asserts something about whether design nodes exist. Nothing looks for them. (`fact:the-answered-question-message-recurred-in-a-third-project-with-the-computation-unchanged`)
② `describe_schema` — its ranking says GOVERNED_BY is no better a fit than sixteen wildcards, when it is the design's primary governance edge and the true answer to the pair being asked about. The rank is computed from endpoint enumeration and presented as modelledness. (`fact:governed-by-is-the-governance-edge-and-describe-schema-can-never-rank-it`)
③ `authored_by` — "deliberately not a traceability edge, so it never enlarges a blast radius". True about propagation, and it reads as "nothing computes on this" at the exact moment an agent decides whether to set `role: approver`, which is the assignment primitive that drives loop debt. (`fact:authored-by-describes-itself-as-inert-and-is-the-assignment-primitive`)

⭐ AND A FOURTH, ALREADY FIXED ONCE, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH ASKING: heal.rs records in its own comment that `unthreaded_cluster` "SPOKE THE WORDS OF UNREACHABILITY AND WALKED SOMETHING NARROWER" — the message claimed disconnection from the design while computing disconnection from a walk covering 1133 of 2413 nodes. Same defect, found by dev_storyflow 2026-08-17, repaired in the sentence. Nothing generalised from it.

THE COMMON SHAPE, stated to be attacked: **reflow2's prose is load-bearing — its own field reports say so — and it is maintained entirely by hand with nothing checking any sentence against the behaviour it describes.** The root-cause skill's own heuristic is that the cause is usually something maintained by hand with nothing checking it; here the hand-maintained thing is the feature.

⚠️ WHY THIS MIGHT BE ONE THING: the failure is invisible by construction. A wrong sentence and a right one both compile, both ship, and the gap only appears when a user acts on the sentence — which is exactly how all four surfaced, each from a different project, none from a test.

⚠️ AND WHY IT MIGHT NOT, which is the honest counter and is strong: these three have three different causes. ① is a message asserting past its data. ② is a ranking function whose criterion does not track the thing it is presented as ranking. ③ is a true sentence that misleads by omission. Only ① is straightforwardly "the prose lies". Grouping them could manufacture a systemic defect out of three ordinary ones — the over-engineering failure this project watches for, and the same reason `dec:idea-the-instruction-layer-runs-ahead-of-the-typed-tool-layer` was REJECTED on 2026-08-31 for a neighbouring grouping. That rejection is evidence against this one.

NOT A COUNT ANYBODY HAS TAKEN: how many tool descriptions and gap texts make a checkable claim about behaviour, and what fraction are currently true. Nobody has looked.","kind":"exploratory","name":"OPEN — three of six chama findings are reflow2 describing itself wrongly. The prose is the acclaimed feature and nothing checks it. Is that one defect or three?","rationale":"WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is cheap enough to be worth naming: the claims in question are a specific and small kind — a sentence asserting what a COMPUTATION does or does not do ("never reached the design", "never enlarges a blast radius", a rank presented as fit). That is narrower than "is the documentation accurate", and it may be testable: a test that asserts the message text alongside the state that produces it would have caught ① and would have failed the day the message was written.

If most load-bearing prose makes no checkable claim, these three are three bugs and this node should be rejected like its predecessor. If a meaningful fraction does, the generative question is "which other sentences assert something about a computation, and which are still true?" — and that is answerable by reading the tool surface rather than by waiting for a fourth project to report it.

⚠️ THE REPAIRS ARE INDEPENDENT OF THE ANSWER. All three are cheap on their own and none waits on this question. Recorded so the fifth instance is recognised rather than diagnosed from scratch — which is precisely what ① cost three separate sessions.","status":"proposed"}
